previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of CVA, tracheostomy, ileostomy, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and prior Pseudomonas pneumonia was admitted from a skilled nursing facility for fever and hypotension. He was found to have sepsis likely from pneumonia and a urinary tract infection caused by Proteus stuartii. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics including vancomycin, meropenem, and ciprofloxacin. His condition improved with stabilization of vital signs, resolution of fever, and decreasing white blood cell count. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic administration. His atrial fibrillation required temporary discontinuation of Coumadin due to supratherapeutic INR, and he was rate-controlled with metoprolol. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. Thrush was treated with nystatin, and his stage III sacral ulcer was managed with wound care and pain control. He was discharged to extended care on a 10-day course of IV and oral antibiotics with close INR and blood sugar monitoring.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ performed the procedure.  Dr. ___,
the attending radiologist, supervised the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  1% buffered lidocaine.

TECHNIQUE:  A pre-procedure timeout was performed.  Using sterile technique
and local anesthesia, the right basilic vein was punctured under direct
ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.  Hard copies of ultrasound
images were obtained before and immediately after establishing intravenous
access are on file.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a guidewire and a
double-lumen PICC line measuring 40 cm in length was then placed through the
peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the distal SVC under fluoroscopic
guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film
of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.  The patient
tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:
Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided single lumen PICC line
placement via the right basilic vein approach.  Final internal length is 40
cm, with the tip positioned in the distal SVC.  The line is ready for use.
